selection_invariants.statement: One topology-independent creation/network declaration remains above all selected transport mechanisms.
Principal identity, runtime session identity and transient transport identity are role-distinct and reconnect only rebinds transport identity while session remains valid.
Peer-hosted browser primary transport is WebRTC DataChannel with WSS signalling and ICE/STUN/TURN traversal.
Peer-hosted transport may fall back to a trusted routing-only WSS relay without moving simulation authority into the relay.
Dedicated-authoritative baseline transport is WSS for browser/native compatibility; clients never self-promote on server loss.
Authentication occurs in a trusted control plane; browser/native public clients use authorization-code plus PKCE and runtime join uses short-lived scoped tickets.
Authentication/session tickets and signalling assertions do not grant SplashMX runtime capabilities.
TLS/signalling/ICE/TURN/suspension/reconnect/server failures map to typed runtime outcomes without becoming canonical state.
Signalling is bounded and cannot import principal, Thing, capability, host-handle, Godot peer or other authority identity.
Peer host is simulation authority but remains untrusted for fairness; dedicated authority is an operated service trust domain.
WebRTC native plugin dependency is not silently required for the v1 dedicated baseline; optional native WebRTC remains a target adapter decision.
ENet/raw UDP is not a browser baseline and WebTransport/custom QUIC remains deferred until a Godot production path is justified.
Browser suspension/reconnect is treated as an ordinary lifecycle transition and may create a new transport identity without replacing principal/session identity.
CI-local connection and framing measurements are mechanism evidence, never product SLOs.
Protected Asset revisions remain indivisible across topology, signalling, relay, reconnect and target projection.
Transport IDs, offers, answers, ICE candidates and TLS/session material are transient runtime context and forbidden canonical identity.
